Do you have the deep functional and technical experience to help implement security solutions that align with our clients’ business objectives? Do you have the expertise to design and deliver solutions for establishing system user's credentials, and processes for applying those credentials to access enterprise systems and applications? If so, read on and apply. Accenture’s more than 2,000 security professionals deliver holistic and proactive security solutions in 47 countries, and we’d love to discuss our open Identity and Access Management (I&AM) Security role with you You Are An engineer who has stayed an engineer. You came up building things, and you have no interest in a career track that takes that away. You're resourceful about how you get there. You know which problems call for a library, which call for a vendor product, and which call for writing the thing yourself. You read the spec instead of guessing what it says. You've debugged something at 2am because you wanted to know why it broke, not because anyone asked. You've shipped code that other people depended on and that you were on the hook for when it broke. You go one layer deeper than the assignment required. You can explain a hard technical idea to someone who doesn't share your background without either condescending or hiding behind jargon. You almost certainly haven't done this specific work before. Very few people have, which is most of why it's interesting. The Work The Forward Deployed Engineer, Agentic Identity Platform is a hands-on technical role. Enterprises are deploying AI agents faster than anyone has figured out how to secure them. An agent authenticates to twelve systems, spawns subagents, calls tools on behalf of a user who left the company last month and holds credentials nobody inventoried. The identity primitives that industry spent twenty years building for humans and service accounts don't cleanly extend to actors that are autonomous, ephemeral, and delegating authority to each other. We're building the platforms that solve this: agent registries, delegated authorization models, runtime attribution, and policy engines that make decisions in single-digit milliseconds. Some of it ships to Fortune 100 clients. Some of it becomes the reference architecture the industry copies.
